claims.verdict: proved as written using the stated classical Stieltjes representations
claims.hypotheses: Finite positive ordinary networks; actual series L plus arbitrary RC or series C plus arbitrary RL; no bypass. Unit reference and seven stated positive-real Laplace samples.

proof_obligations.RC: Second difference kills the linear L term and is nonnegative on every Stieltjes kernel.
proof_obligations.RL: s*Z is a degree-at-most-two polynomial plus positive Stieltjes terms. Sixth difference kills that polynomial; the target residual is negative.
proof_obligations.transfer: h<0 and delta<=1/2 give |Z-ZH|<=4*delta; both chosen rational margins satisfy a strict stencil contradiction.
proof_obligations.support: The arbitrary one-L bridge violates convexity and prevents promotion from a series support class to a full-resistor-core skeleton.
proof_obligations.boundaries: Zero Stieltjes coefficients and pole-at-zero terms retain weak signs. Open/short ports are directly separated.

claims.evidence: Exact rational kernel numerator identities, strict transfer slack, 24 series graphs/168 samples plus three nonregular-bridge samples; source dependencies inherited from the preceding Stieltjes proofs.
claims.formal_scope: Written universal proof and exact arithmetic only; no added Lean coverage

claims.verdict: proved as written by project self-review, with the explicit finite branch phasor-solution hypothesis
claims.hypotheses: Exactly one L, arbitrary C/R, finite positive DC and infinity impedance, omega>0, finite nonzero purely imaginary impedance and a finite branch phasor solution.

proof_obligations.power: Zero real input power forces all positive resistor currents to vanish; resistor-connected potentials agree.
proof_obligations.DC: Finite DC requires an R+L path; its only L joins the distinct terminal resistor components.
proof_obligations.infinity: Positive infinity endpoint forbids a C-only port path; finite infinity endpoint requires an R+C path.
proof_obligations.KCL_pairing: Each terminal capacitor component contains exactly one L endpoint. The equal-potential pairing makes every C drop zero, contradicting the R+C path. The opposite pairing gives I=-IL and Z=-i*omega*L.
proof_obligations.degeneracies: Singleton components, coincident terminal/L endpoints and floating C components are addressed by the same weighted-Laplacian energy identity.
proof_obligations.one_C: Physical s->1/s exchanges L/C with reciprocal values and conjugates the positive imaginary frequency; both endpoint hypotheses are preserved.
proof_obligations.limits: This exact loss-free theorem supplies no quantitative positive-real sample margin.

claims.evidence: 24 exact physical controls with 48 zero-resistor-current checks. Hughes Lemma 9 is consistent with the power step; the full component-pairing proof is written locally.
claims.priority: Not claimed novel; broad priority and independent/formal review remain open

claims.verdict: proved as written; inverse and finite controls computationally verified

proof_obligations.identity: Cross polynomial degree <=q+2; enough distinct roots force identity; PH and QH are coprime since QH-PH=5-s and PH(5)=169.
proof_obligations.fiber: Degree three gives a segment. Degree four gives a four-vertex polygon, including a vertex with negative multiplier middle coefficient.
proof_obligations.sample_bound: Normalization and nonnegativity give P(s)+Q(s)<=max(1,s^q). Exact inverse weighted row norms give the stated C3,C4.
proof_obligations.nonnegative_repair: The affine projection need not be nonnegative. Mixing it with a displayed interior fiber vector with min coefficient rho gives an actual fiber vector at distance <=epsilon/(rho+epsilon).
proof_obligations.scope: No physical graph is excluded, and no resonant/endpoint denominator bound is inferred.

claims.evidence: Both inverse products; independent polynomial division; independent feasible boundary-intersection enumeration of the polygon vertices; 164 projection and 91 barycentric fiber controls; six corruptions rejected

claims.verdict: proved as written; 2130 finite graph-map controls passed

proof_obligations.lift: Split endpoints; wire each original vertex to its anchor; keep original R core on anchors and open all unused edges. Quotient reconstructs every edge and fixed port.
proof_obligations.arbitrary_R: Uses the earlier written resistor-only elimination; this phase supplies placement consolidation after that reduction.
proof_obligations.continuity: For each positive sample, bounded minimizing potentials have vanishing wire drops; the limiting energy is the contracted energy, with unique port potential from the unit source term.
proof_obligations.boundaries: Wire and open resistor faces are essential. Finite-positive-only certificates must be uniform to extend to them.
proof_obligations.complexity: Five template distributions consolidate cases but do not remove the continuous parameter/boundary burden.

claims.verdict: refuted by exact physical families as written

proof_obligations.physical: Retained exact Hughes circuit plus an actual series C, L or parallel RLC one-port, all positive.
proof_obligations.counts: Six-reactive degree-three endpoint examples; seven-reactive degree-four resonance example. These are not at-most-four-reactive counterexamples.
proof_obligations.bounds: At positive samples error <=4*epsilon for endpoints, <=epsilon for resonance. Resonant error squared is exactly 2/(1+2epsilon+2epsilon^2).
proof_obligations.implication: Passivity plus reduced degree and real-sample/coefficient proximity alone does not justify transfer at DC, infinity or a resonant common-factor zero.
